# swiftpm

<!-- The reference table below this banner is regenerated by `make generate`. Handwritten prose below the table lives in internal/support/prose/. -->

This page explains how Bomly builds a dependency graph for `swiftpm` projects: the detector chain it runs, what that chain needs, and what it can report.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Package manager | `swiftpm` |
| Ecosystem | `swift` |
| Detector chain | `swiftpm-native-detector`, `swiftpm-detector`, `syft-detector` |
| Evidence patterns | `Package.resolved`, `.package.resolved`, `.swiftpm/xcode/package.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved`, `project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved`, `Package.swift` |
| Multi-module resolution | No |
| Install-first support | No |
| Remediation hints | None |
| Commands the chain may run | `swift`. The Syft fallback is built in; the lite build runs an external `syft` from `PATH` instead. |

## Source details

Bomly reads registry, remote source-control, and local source-control origins
from SwiftPM resolved data. Older resolved files use `repositoryURL`, which is
SwiftPM's source-control field. Remote source-control packages remain eligible
for vulnerability matching because the repository URL is their Swift package
identity. An unrecognized pin kind stays unknown.
